headline: VISIBLE GOLD Struck in Both Drill Holes — Metals Creek Hits High-Grade Quartz Veins on Timmins Porcupine-Destor Break
snippet: Metals Creek Resources (TSXV: MEK) confirmed visible gold in the first two holes of its Ogden Gold Project drill program in Timmins, Ontario — a 50/50 JV with Discovery Silver. Mineralization is hosted along the prolific Porcupine-Destor Break with multiple generations of quartz veins and strong albitization.

headline: DRILLS TURNING in Yukon: 5,000-Metre Copper-Gold Expedition Launches at AZ and Birch Porphyry Targets
snippet: Yukon Metals Corp. (CSE: YMC) kicked off its 2026 field season June 4 with drills turning at the AZ and Birch copper-gold properties — 2,000m at the AZ porphyry target and 3,000m at Birch skarn. 3D induced-polarization geophysics is already underway to vector on the highest-priority drill collars.

headline: CAMECO SPENDS $115.75M to Lift Cigar Lake Stake to 57.4% as TEPCO Exits World's Top Uranium Mine
snippet: Cameco and Orano Canada agreed June 1 to buy TEPCO Resources' 5% interest in the Cigar Lake Joint Venture for $115.75 million, lifting Cameco's stake from ~54.5% to 57.418%. The deal consolidates ownership at one of the world's highest-grade uranium mines ahead of a structural demand surge from new reactor builds.

headline: Copper One Completes Redonda Copper Acquisition from Uranium One, Expands B.C. Footprint
snippet: Copper One Resources completed the purchase of a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper property from Uranium One Mining Corp., with mineral titles formally transferred June 2, 2026. The deal adds a new copper exploration asset in British Columbia as the junior pivots toward base-metal growth.

headline: GOLD RANGE $4,300–$4,800 in June — Expert Panel Split on Whether $5,000 Is Still in Sight
snippet: Three precious-metals specialists forecast gold trading between $4,300 and $4,800 through June with potential seasonal softening on jewelry demand lulls, while silver is seen ranging $72–$88. One portfolio manager at Midas Funds warns of a 0–5% near-term pullback from current $4,447 levels before any year-end push toward $5,000.

headline: SIXTH YEAR OF SILVER DEFICITS: China Absorbs 790+ Tonnes in Early 2026 as Global Visible Inventory Drains
snippet: Silver enters its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026 with China importing over 790 tonnes in early 2026, driven by solar panel production. COMEX, LBMA, and Shanghai inventories are declining simultaneously — nearly a billion ounces have vanished from visible global stocks since 2021.

headline: GDX FLAT YTD at $85 While Spot Gold Holds $4,450 — The Miner Valuation Gap That Won't Close
snippet: With GDX trading at $85.18 and essentially flat year-to-date while spot gold holds near $4,450, the anticipated miner catch-up trade has stalled heading into June. Analysis argues share prices still don't reflect the margin expansion implied by current gold levels, keeping the sector cheaper than fundamentals suggest.

headline: CHINA REWRITES THE MAP: 2026 Licensing Rules Add Samarium, Gadolinium, Lutetium to Rare Earth Export Controls
snippet: China's 2026 Export Licensing Catalogue expansions now require permits for samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium compounds, extending a tightening grip on heavy rare earth elements. Outside China, price spikes of up to 600% have been recorded on some controlled materials, while licensing approval rates for European buyers have fallen below 25% in certain sectors.

headline: BATTERY BOOM RESCUES LITHIUM: Energy Storage Set to Hit 31% of Total Consumption in 2026, Up From 23%
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery storage is reshaping lithium's demand picture for 2026, with the storage segment projected to represent 31% of total consumption versus 23% in 2025. Brokers see storage demand growing 55% this year, potentially pulling the market out of the oversupply slump that kept mines on care-and-maintenance.

headline: Copper Slides 1.5% to $6.42/lb June 5 — Supply Deficit Thesis Collides With Tariff-Driven Volatility
snippet: Copper dropped 1.47% to $6.42/lb on June 5 as markets weigh a structural deficit against tariff uncertainty. J.P. Morgan forecasts a 330,000-tonne refined copper shortfall in 2026 while Chile — the world's largest producer — posted its weakest April output in 23 years, setting the stage for continued two-way price swings.
